Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short, firm answer up front: Redwood does not use customer-provided prompts, responses, documents, or attachments from your account to train or fine-tune our public models. That guarantee applies to hosted API customers by default; for Dedicated and Private deployments we provide controls that prevent telemetry collection entirely.

Caveats and nuance (summary):
- \"Do not train\" scope: we never add identifiable customer content (raw prompts, attachments, or generated outputs tied to a customer account) into model training corpora or weight updates.
- Service-improvement telemetry: we may collect aggregated, non‑identifiable telemetry (e.g., token counts, latency histograms, error rates) and high-level anonymized feature usage for product quality improvements. This telemetry is not linked back to prompt text.
- Logs and retention: default retention windows (hosted): request/response logs retained for 30 days; diagnostic traces (detailed traces, full request payloads used for debugging) retained for 90 days; attachments stored for up to 90 days unless removed earlier. Customers can request earlier deletion.
- Legal and billing exceptions: records required by law (e.g., subpoena) or billing dispute investigations may be retained until resolution. We will notify customers for exceptional holds when permitted by law.
- Deletion process: upon a verified deletion request Redwood initiates a deletion workflow: active indices and caches are purged within 48 hours; background archival systems are purged within 30 days; immutable backups may be pruned according to our backup retention policy (typically 90 days) unless otherwise negotiated.
- Private/Dedicated options: Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured with a no-telemetry mode and customer-managed logging so that none of the above telemetry leaves your VPC.

I attached our SOC2 evidence checklist and a high-level dataflow diagram for your security team. Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through any of these points.

Best,
